messages:
maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up — we've been getting multiple p99 latency complaints since ~02:10 UTC for the hosted /v1/generate endpoint. Several customer tickets (large seq workloads) and internal synthetic canaries show p95 up ~1.8x and p99 spikes to 4-6s. :rotating_light:

sam (support): Customer reported timeouts when using streaming with long context (~>1k tokens). They included a couple of request IDs: r_0a3f2c, r_0a3f7d. Said this started after yesterday afternoon (their local time).

devon (eng-sre): Looking at Grafana — cluster-level p95 jumped at 02:07 UTC, p99 waveform shows repeated spikes correlating with high iowait on the inference node group (inference-eu-west-2-pool). CPU idle fine, but softirq and iowait up. Putting queries: "sum(rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total[1m])) by (instance)" — top nodes show anomalous I/O stalls.

anya (eng-infra): We rolled a GPU driver update to 535.54 on that pool in the 01:30–01:50 UTC window (automated image update job). deploy-bot logs:
```
deploy-bot: gpu-driver-upgrade v525->v535 applied to group inference-eu-west-2-pool at 01:42 UTC
```
Noticed a small number of nodes failed a post-upgrade smoke test and were cycled.

lia (eng-ml): Model serving logs show many repeated KV cache misses and longer step times per token on those same nodes. Per-request token generation time bumped from ~35ms/token to 120ms/token during spikes.

maria (eng-runtime): Can we correlate GPU metrics? devon, do you have nvidia-smi stats + NVMe metrics?

devon (eng-sre): Pulling metrics now. NVMe avg latency (ns) from node exporter jumped coincident with driver roll. Also seeing increased NVMe read latencies ~3-15ms (baseline <0.5ms). dstat shows high await. Collecting `iostat -x 1 5` and `nvidia-smi dmon` dumps.

ops-bot: Alert: p99 latency > 3s for /v1/generate on inference-eu-west-2-pool (threshold breached at 02:09 UTC).

sam (support): Customers asking for ETA / workaround. Any temporary routing we can do?

anya (eng-infra): Immediate candidate mitigations:
- Roll back GPU driver on a small canary subset to v525 (fast).
- Move NVMe-heavy tenants off the affected pool (hot-shard separation).
- Temporarily scale up dedicated capacity for paid customers.
- Tune I/O scheduler / kernel knob if NVMe stalls persist.

maria (eng-runtime): Also can lower max_batch_size and reduce batching window on the runtime for that pool to limit tail amplification while we diagnose. Lia, can you test reduced batch config?

lia (eng-ml): Yep. Running canary with max_batch_size=4 and batch_timeout=10ms now against one node. Will post perf numbers in ~5m.

devon (eng-sre): Repro steps I used to generate similar spike locally:
```bash
# run synthetic long-context generator load against specific node
python infra/tools/loadgen.py --target https://node-12.inference.internal:443/v1/generate \
  --model gpt-redwood-1 --seq 1024 --concurrency 6 --requests 500 --streaming
```
This reproduces increased per-token latency after ~50–100 requests when NVMe stalls triggered.

maria (eng-runtime): Nice repro. Can anyone share node-level `dmesg` around the time of spike? Looking for NVRM Xid or kernel messages.

anya (eng-infra): Found kernel log snippet from a cycled node: 
```
[Feb15 01:41:13] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, pid=0
[Feb15 01:41:15] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
[Feb15 01:41:16] nvme nvme0: aborting command 0x...
```
That looks like GPU driver + NVMe interaction (possibly driver changed DMA patterns).

devon (eng-sre): We also saw kernel preemption events and higher softirq -> could be the new driver using different PCIe transactions causing device starvation.

maria (eng-runtime): Priority plan:
1) Anya to roll back GPU driver on a canary of 3 nodes (not all) to v525 and see p99 behavior. (ETA 20m) :hammer_and_wrench:
2) Lia reduces batch config on remaining nodes (in progress).
3) Devon to isolate NVMe IO-heavy VMs and run fio to characterize latency under driver versions.
4) If rollback helps, stage full rollback during low traffic window and then reopen a safe driver upgrade with more IO testing.

anya (eng-infra): Starting canary rollback now on nodes node-12/node-17/node-19. Commands: 
```bash
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-525 -y
systemctl restart gpu-runtime.service
# check smoke
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,timestamp --format=csv
```
Will report rollback results in 15m.

deploy-bot: image-patch job started for inference-eu-west-2-pool (rollback-canaried).

sam (support): Notified affected customers that we're investigating and offered temporary routing to dedicated instances where possible.

lia (eng-ml): Canary with reduced batched runtime now shows p99 reduced from 4.8s -> 2.1s on that node; per-token time improved to ~60ms. Not perfect but better.

devon (eng-sre): fio test results comparing drivers (short summary):
- v525: 99th latency 0.6ms read
- v535: 99th latency 4.9ms read (under synthetic mixed rw 70/30 workload at 16k io depth)
So NVMe tail latency definitely regressed with v535 in our environment.

maria (eng-runtime): Given that rollback canary + batching tweak brought p99 down significantly, proceed to roll back remainder during maintenance window. Also create routing rule to divert heavy long-context customers to dedicated capacity until we fully validate.

anya (eng-infra): Rolling remaining nodes tonight 23:00 UTC; will hold driver upgrade in staging until we reproduce in lab. I'll also file a support ticket with the GPU vendor including NVMe traces.

devon (eng-sre): Follow-up items (I'll own):
- collect full fio configs + kernel logs and file vendor ticket.
- bake NVMe isolation playbook and changed scheduling (consider BFQ or mq-deadline tuned).
- add pre-upgrade smoke that includes heavier NVMe/mixed RW profile.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll open an incidents postmortem template after rollback. We should include: timeline, customer impact, root cause hypothesis (driver+NVMe interaction), mitigations, and longer-term fixes (improve preflight tests, adjust runtime batching heuristics, node isolation).

sam (support): I'll follow up with customers once we finish rollback and confirm p99 stabilizes.

anya (eng-infra): Canary rollback completed — preliminary grafana shows p99 on those nodes back to baseline within ~6 minutes post-rollback. I'll keep monitoring and post final metric graphs.

maria (eng-runtime): Great work. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene in 2 hours in #incidents to confirm closure unless anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
